---
title: "Lab 03 — Generalized linear models in R"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
bw <- read_csv("data/birthwt.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(race = factor(race, levels = c("white", "black", "other")),
         ptd  = as.integer(ptl > 0)) %>%
  as.data.frame()
ships <- read_csv("data/ships.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% as.data.frame()
fit <- glm(low ~ age + lwt + race + smoke + ptd + ht + ui, family = binomial, data = bw)
fit_nohist <- update(fit, . ~ . - ptd - ht - ui)
set.seed(2027)
train_id <- c(sample(which(bw$low == 1), 39), sample(which(bw$low == 0), 87))
train <- bw[train_id, ]
test  <- bw[-train_id, ]
fit_tr <- glm(low ~ age + lwt + race + smoke + ptd + ht + ui, family = binomial, data = train)
p_tr <- fitted(fit_tr)
p_te <- predict(fit_tr, newdata = test, type = "response")
rates <- function(p, y, cut) {
  yhat <- as.integer(p >= cut)
  c(sens = mean(yhat[y == 1] == 1), spec = mean(yhat[y == 0] == 0),
    acc = mean(yhat == y))
}
sh <- subset(ships, service > 0)
sh$type   <- factor(sh$type)
sh$year   <- factor(sh$year)
sh$period <- factor(sh$period)
fit_p <- glm(incidents ~ type + year + period + offset(log(service)),
             family = poisson, data = sh)
fit_q <- update(fit_p, family = quasipoisson)
fit_nb <- suppressWarnings(
  glm.nb(incidents ~ type + year + period + offset(log(service)), data = sh))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab03", title = "Generalized linear models in R", open = c("q6", "q10"))
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1  = "In the birthwt logistic model, the odds ratio for smoke and its meaning are…",
  q2  = "The 95% profile-likelihood interval for the odds ratio of hypertension (ht) is…",
  q3  = "The likelihood-ratio test of the medical-history block (ptd, ht, ui) gives…",
  q4  = "If missing a low-birth-weight baby costs 3 times as much as an unnecessary visit, the cost-optimal threshold for calibrated probabilities is…",
  q5  = "With the threshold of the previous question, the test-set sensitivity and specificity are…",
  q6  = "The Youden threshold chosen on the test set is 0.13, with test sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.44. Why can these numbers not be reported as the performance of the classifier?",
  q7  = "In the ships Poisson model with offset log(service), the rate ratio for period 75 vs 60 means…",
  q8  = "The Pearson estimate of the dispersion for the ships Poisson model is…",
  q9  = "glm.nb() on ships warns that the iteration limit was reached and reports k (\"theta\") of about 50000. This means…",
  q10 = "Which model would you report for ships (Poisson, quasi-Poisson or negative binomial), and why?"
)
```

## What you will do

Check the numbers from the lab, then answer the questions. The data and models are already loaded: `bw`, `fit` (logistic model on all births), `fit_nohist` (without `ptd`, `ht`, `ui`), `train`, `test`, `p_tr`, `p_te`, the function `rates()`, and for the ships `sh`, `fit_p` (Poisson), `fit_q` (quasi-Poisson) and `fit_nb` (negative binomial). Finish by downloading the `.txt` file.

## Logistic regression for low birth weight

```{r or-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=3}
round(exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit), confint(fit))), 3)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("About 2.33. The odds of a low-birth-weight baby for smokers are about 2.3 times those of non-smokers of the same age, weight, race and medical history.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("About 2.33. Smokers are 2.3 times as likely to have a low-birth-weight baby."),
  answer("About 0.85. Smoking raises the probability of low birth weight by 0.85."),
  answer("About 1.06. That is the smallest effect smoking can have."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("(1.64, 27.26)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("(1.58, 24.95)"),
  answer("(0.46, 3.22)"),
  answer("(4.91, 7.67)"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Testing a block of predictors

```{r lr-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=4}
anova(fit_nohist, fit, test = "Chisq")
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("LR = 17.74 on 3 df, p about 0.0005: the history block is needed.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("LR = 196.83 on 180 df: the model fits well, so the block is needed."),
  answer("LR = 6.41 on 2 df, p about 0.04."),
  answer("LR = 17.74 on 183 df, p close to 1: the block is not needed."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## From probabilities to decisions

Remember: the threshold is chosen on the training data; the test data are used once, to evaluate.

```{r thr-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=5}
c_star <- 1 / (1 + 3)
rates(p_te, test$low, c_star)
table(predicted = as.integer(p_te >= c_star), observed = test$low)
```

```{r q4}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  answer("0.25, whatever the prevalence of low birth weight.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.75, because missed cases are three times as costly."),
  answer("0.31, the prevalence of low birth weight in the sample."),
  answer("0.50, because the probabilities are calibrated."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q5}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q5"]],
  answer("Sensitivity 0.70 and specificity 0.60.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Sensitivity 0.40 and specificity 0.81."),
  answer("Sensitivity 0.67 and specificity 0.78."),
  answer("Sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.44."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q6}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q6"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "The threshold was tuned with the test labels, so...",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Poisson regression and overdispersion

```{r disp-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
round(exp(cbind(RR = coef(fit_p), confint(fit_p))), 3)
X2 <- sum(residuals(fit_p, type = "pearson")^2)
c(phi_hat = X2 / df.residual(fit_p), k = fit_nb$theta)
```

```{r q7}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q7"]],
  answer("Ships operating in 1975–79 have an incident rate about 1.47 times that in 1960–74, for ships of the same type and construction year (95% CI about 1.17 to 1.85).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Ships operating in 1975–79 have about 1.47 more incidents per month of service."),
  answer("Ships operating in 1975–79 have 1.47 times as many incidents, whatever their months of service."),
  answer("The rate in 1975–79 is 0.38 times the rate in 1960–74."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q8}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q8"]],
  answer("About 1.69, the Pearson statistic 42.28 divided by 25 residual df.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("About 1.55, the residual deviance divided by its df."),
  answer("About 38.70, the residual deviance."),
  answer("About 0.04, the p-value of the deviance test."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q9}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q9"]],
  answer("The estimate of k runs off to infinity, so the negative binomial collapses to the Poisson: the extra variance is not of the form mu^2 / k.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("A huge k means huge overdispersion, so the negative binomial is essential."),
  answer("The negative binomial fits much better, because its AIC is larger."),
  answer("The algorithm failed, so the data cannot be overdispersed."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q10}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q10"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "phi-hat is..., k-hat is..., so I report...",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
